samples: This program reads `data/sales.csv`, requiring each row to have a region, a product and a numeric amount, and it stops with an error naming the line if any row is missing a field or has a non-numeric amount. It then adds up the amounts per region, prints the totals to the console from highest to lowest, and saves the same ranking as `data/report.csv`, overwriting any existing file. It can only touch files under the `data` folder, and region names are written to the report as-is, so a name containing a comma would break the CSV layout.

This program reads `data/sales.csv`, checks that every row has a region, a product and a numeric amount, and stops with an error naming the offending line if any row is bad. It then adds up the amounts for each region, prints the totals from highest to lowest, and saves the same totals as a two-column CSV at `data/report.csv`. The file locations are fixed rather than configurable, and its permissions are limited to the console and the `data` folder, so it suits a simple one-off summary of a file in that exact place and would need changes for anything more flexible.

This program reads `data/sales.csv`, expecting each row to have region, product and amount columns, and trims the text and converts the amount to a decimal. It adds up the amounts for each region, prints the regional totals from highest to lowest, and writes them to `data/report.csv` as a two-column CSV, overwriting any existing report. The input path is fixed, it can only touch files under the `data` folder, and it stops with an error naming the line if any row is missing a field or has a non-numeric amount, so one bad row means no report at all.

This program reads `data/sales.csv`, checks that every row has a region, product and numeric amount, and stops with an error naming the line number of the first bad row (or an I/O error if the file can't be read or isn't valid CSV). If the file is clean, it adds up the amounts per region, prints the totals to the console from highest to lowest, and writes the same totals to `data/report.csv`, replacing any existing report. The input and output paths are fixed in the program, and it is only permitted to use the console and the `data` folder, so it is safe to run but not configurable without editing it.

This program reads `data/sales.csv`, requiring each row to have a region, a product, and a numeric amount, and it stops with an error naming the line if any row is missing a field or has a non-numeric amount. It then adds up the amounts per region, prints the totals from highest to lowest, and saves them as a two-column CSV report in `data/report.csv`, overwriting any existing report. It only touches files in the `data` folder and prints to the console, so it is a small and safe tool, but it is all-or-nothing: one bad row means no output at all.
